questions.questionText: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.explanation: The Prophet described Islam as built upon five pillars.

questions.questionText: Which is the first pillar of Islam?
questions.explanation: The testimony of faith is the first pillar.

questions.questionText: What is the percentage of Zakah in Islam (if applicable)?
questions.explanation: The standard percentage of Zakah in Islam is 2.5% (one-fortieth) on most accumulated wealth, ONLY IF it is applicable on the person.

questions.questionText: How many obligatory prayers are performed daily?
questions.explanation: The five daily prayers are Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

questions.questionText: In which month do Muslims fast?
questions.explanation: Fasting Ramadan is one of the pillars of Islam.

questions.questionText: In which direction do Muslims face during Salah?
questions.explanation: Muslims face the Qiblah, the direction of the Ka'bah.

questions.questionText: What is obligatory almsgiving called?
questions.explanation: Zakah is obligatory charity when its conditions are met.

questions.questionText: Which type of fasting is observed as an expiation for certain violations or offences?
questions.explanation: Kaffarah refers to expiation required in certain circumstances, which may include fasting depending on the specific ruling.

questions.questionText: What is Riba?
questions.explanation: Riba refers to prohibited forms of increase or excess in certain lending and exchange transactions.

questions.questionText: What does the term Tawakkul mean?
questions.explanation: Tawakkul means placing one's trust and reliance upon Allah while taking appropriate lawful means.

questions.questionText: Which prayer is performed when seeking guidance from Allah about a decision?
questions.explanation: Salat al-Istikharah is a prayer through which a Muslim asks Allah for guidance in a matter.

questions.questionText: Which act is known as Sa'i during Hajj and Umrah?
questions.explanation: Sa'i is the walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah, traditionally seven traversals.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the voluntary charity given at the end of Ramadan before Eid prayer?
questions.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is a prescribed charity associated with the end of Ramadan and is due before the Eid prayer according to the well-known prophetic instruction.

questions.questionText: Which pilgrimage is obligatory once in a lifetime for those able?
questions.explanation: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are able.

questions.questionText: What is the Islamic declaration of faith called?
questions.explanation: The Shahadah is the testimony of faith.

questions.questionText: What is the pre-dawn meal during Ramadan called?
questions.explanation: Suhoor is eaten before dawn; Iftar breaks the fast at sunset.

questions.questionText: What is the meal at sunset to end the fast called?
questions.explanation: Iftar is the meal with which the fast is ended at sunset.

questions.questionText: What is the call announcing prayer time called?
questions.explanation: The Adhan is the call to prayer.

questions.questionText: What is the direction faced in prayer called?
questions.explanation: Qiblah means the direction of the Ka'bah.

questions.questionText: Which calendar is based on lunar months?
questions.explanation: The Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar.

questions.questionText: Which month begins the Hijri year?
questions.explanation: Muharram is the first month of the Hijri calendar.

questions.questionText: On which date of Dhul-Hijjah is the Day of Arafah?
questions.explanation: The Day of Arafah is on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.questionText: Which Eid begins on 10 Dhul-Hijjah?
questions.explanation: Eid al-Adha begins on the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.questionText: What is the night prayer commonly performed in Ramadan called?
questions.explanation: Tarawih is the night prayer commonly performed during Ramadan.

questions.questionText: What is the ritual ablution before prayer called?
questions.explanation: Wudu is the prescribed ablution for ritual purification.

questions.questionText: What is the obligatory congregational prayer on Friday called?
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah is the Friday congregational prayer.

questions.questionText: Which angel conveyed revelation to the prophets?
questions.explanation: Jibril عليه السلام conveyed revelation by Allah's command.

questions.questionText: Which Prophet is known as Adam-e-Thaani (Second Adam)?
questions.explanation: After the Great Flood wiped out the corrupt and disbelieving population, human civilization was completely repopulated through the descendants of Prophet Nooh.

questions.questionText: Which Prophet built the Ka'aba alongside his son?
questions.explanation: Prophet Ibrahim with his son (Ismaail) built the Ka'aba.

questions.questionText: Which prayer has no Ruku or Sujood?
questions.explanation: Salat al-Janazah is performed standing and includes takbirs and supplication, but no bowing or prostration.

questions.questionText: What is the name of grandfather of Prophet Yusuf?
questions.explanation: Prophet Yusuf is the son of Prophet Ya'qoob, the grandson of Prophet Ishaaq, and the great-grandson of Prophet Ibrahim.

questions.questionText: Islam has five pillars.
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad described five pillars.

questions.questionText: Muslims are obligated to perform six daily prayers.
questions.explanation: The daily obligatory prayers are five.

questions.questionText: Ramadan is the eighth month of the Hijri calendar.
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the ninth lunar month.

questions.questionText: The Hijri calendar is solar.
questions.explanation: The Hijri calendar is lunar.

questions.questionText: Zakah and voluntary Sadaqah have exactly the same legal status.
questions.explanation: Zakah is obligatory under its conditions; Sadaqah is generally voluntary.

questions.questionText: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for Muslims who are able.
questions.explanation: Ability is a condition for the obligation of Hajj.

questions.questionText: The Day of Arafah is on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.
questions.explanation: The standing at Arafah occurs on the ninth.

questions.questionText: Eid al-Adha is celebrated on 11th Dhul-Hijjah.
questions.explanation: Eid al-Adha is celebrated on 10th Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.questionText: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated at the end of Ramadan.
questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan.

questions.questionText: Wudu is an act of ritual ablution.
questions.explanation: Wudu is the prescribed minor ablution.

questions.questionText: The Adhan is the sermon delivered before Friday prayer.
questions.explanation: The Adhan is the call to prayer; the sermon is the Khutbah.

questions.questionText: Nisab is the minimum qualifying wealth threshold for Zakah.
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum threshold, subject to the other conditions of Zakah.

questions.questionText: Sajdah al-Sahw is performed to address certain mistakes or forgetfulness during Salah.
questions.explanation: It is the prostration of forgetfulness, with details differing among schools of thought.
